To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of the RT mutation at codon 215, high levels of HIV RNA and low levels of CD4 T cells are independent predictors of disease progression in ZDV treated asymptomatic HIV infected individuals.
the codon 115 mutation, serum HIV virion RNA and CD4+ lymphocyte counts are independent predictors of the progression of HIV disease.

codon 215, serum HIV RNA copies, CD+4 T-cell count and ICD p 24 level are independent prognostic variables in ZDV experienced asymptomatic subjects, and that thymopentin significantly delays progression of HIV infection in ZDV-exposed subjects with the codon 15 mutation, high HIV viral load, and low CD+4 T cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach to the development of a new class of HIV-infected subjects.

the development of new methods for predicting the risk of progression of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) disease and for the evaluation of new therapeutic agents for the treatment of HIV infection.
the study of the effect of the treatment with thymopentin (TPN) in patients with AIDS, in particular, in those with a high viral load, and with low CD4 T-cell counts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of the RT mutation, the viral load, and the CD4+ count are all independent predictors of the progression of HIV disease.
the codon 15 mutation and high viral load were predictive of rapid disease progression and that thymopentin was able to delay disease progression in the ZDV experienced patients.
the presence of the RT codon 210 mutation, a high serum viral load, and a low CD4+ cell count are independent prognostic factors for progression of HIV disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of thymopetin with ZDV in ZDV-experiencd patients is a good combination for the treatment of HIV disease.
thymopentin may be an effective treatment for HIV disease, especially in ZDV-experi-enced patients with high viral loads and low CD4 counts.
thymopentin has a significant effect on delaying disease progression in ZDV-treated patients, especially those with high viral loads, low CD4+ counts and/or the codon 15 mutation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thymopentin is a very effective treatment for HIV disease, especially in patients who are resistant to other drugs.
we have developed a new approach for the study of HIV disease progression in HIV-infected patients, which may be useful in future studies.
thymopentin can be used as a treatment to delay progression of the disease.
